speaker: TICKET
text: Aurelio Cruel entered the sixth race himself. The announcement came from Isla Gloria at breakfast. His Grace would personally defend the honor of the Grand Prix in the Bridge of Kings, a crossing of the floating road between the island's eastern harbor and the old naval fort. Tank looked at the photograph of the course. Nigga, that's water with opinions.

speaker: TICKET
text: The road had been assembled from broad linked platforms, each wide enough for two cars, stretching across a sheltered bay. Boats held the outer sections steady. At the far end, a steep ramp climbed onto the fort's quay. The drivers would cross twice, circle the island's coastal road and finish at the palace gate. Nero studied the picture. It used to be a ceremonial crossing.

speaker: TICKET
text: Slow. Flags. Music. Nigga made everything a threat, I said. Yes. Celadon stood beside him, arms folded. The platforms can carry the cars. The danger is what he asks the drivers to do on them. I looked toward the harbor, where the Sovereign Sun now flew its old white bird above the bridge.

speaker: TICKET
text: Celadon had reclaimed the ship in every way that mattered to the people who worked aboard it. The duke still claimed to own it. He also claimed I had ruined the winter garden, which was technically true in enough places to make arguing tedious. Tank stood at the dock counting the cars going aboard.

speaker: TICKET
text: "Nigga, why we bringing a boat to a car race?" "Because the road in the water," I said. "And why the road in the water?" "Because that nigga owns an island." "So when you own it, we fixing that?" Shawna looked over her shoulder. "Nigga, he'll put another road higher up and race both." "See?" Tank said to Bruno. "That nigga ain't a solution.

speaker: TICKET
text: That nigga's more geography." Bruno laughed and ducked beneath the gangway frame. We took the flagship to the race. Nigga, if somebody steals a man's boat and that man gets it back, you ride with the man. The whole crew came aboard in the morning. Lark and Mateo loaded the Lamborghini. Tank brought the replacement black coupe. Porsche brought her Ferrari.

speaker: TICKET
text: Cassius drove the White Heron onto the lower deck with Nero beside him. Inez arrived in red and kissed Cassius before handing him his gloves, a gesture so ordinary now that both their fathers looked away to give it room. Shawna carried her music in a blue case. Rehearsal after? I asked. Victory after. Then rehearsal. Nigga, order matters. It does.

speaker: TICKET
text: We sailed into Isla Gloria's harbor with the ship's bell ringing. People crowded the quay. They saw Celadon on the bridge, saw Nero standing beside him and began cheering before they even found me on the deck. I liked that. Then they found me. Nigga, I liked that too. The duke waited at the starting area in a green racing suit.

speaker: TICKET
text: His car was black and gold, long, low and ugly with money. He wore no mask of courtesy now. The white streaks in his hair stood out sharply against the dark suit, and his eyes followed me with a kind of hunger that had forgotten how to look charming. You brought stolen property to my island, he said. Celadon stepped forward.

speaker: TICKET
text: I brought my ship home. Aurelio looked at him. For a moment I saw the old habit in his face: speak sharply, summon a guard, return the man to a room. Then he saw Nero. Cassius. Odette's officers on the quay. The cameras. The crowd pressing close enough to hear every word. He swallowed the command. Nigga, it looked painful.

speaker: TICKET
text: The race, he said, will proceed. I stood beside my Lamborghini. Good. You been talking for three weeks. His jaw tightened. You think these people love you. I looked around. A woman held up a loaf of bread from the bakery. Julian stood beside her, waving both arms. Alina stood with Mercedes and Porsche on the viewing platform.

speaker: TICKET
text: Rocco wore a blue shirt with my face on it and looked delighted to have found a profitable form of courage. Nigga, I said, ask them. He didn't. We lined up at the floating road. Six cars entered. Inez and Cassius had chosen to race.

speaker: TICKET
text: Adrian joined too, along with a veteran driver named Sabine Cross, forty-one, who had told a reporter she considered Aiden impossible but wanted to confirm it at close range. I respected scientific curiosity. The first horn sounded. The platforms moved gently beneath our wheels. Water shone on both sides.

speaker: TICKET
text: The road ahead rose and fell in long shallow motions, never quite still, making distance a thing you had to feel as much as see. The second horn sounded. The duke looked across at me. I smiled. The third horn sent us forward. His black car surged first. Mine came beside it.

speaker: TICKET
text: We reached the first joint together, wheels striking the metal seam with a hard ringing sound. The platform dipped beneath us, rose again, and the sea came up level with the lower edge of my window. Nigga, that got my attention. Aurelio knew the course. He had practiced.

speaker: TICKET
text: His car moved with ugly confidence, taking the center of each platform and forcing me toward the edge. I let him have the first bend. Stayed close. Watched the way the floating road lifted before the next joint. Behind us, Inez and Cassius ran side by side in red and white, their cars bright against the blue water. Sabine held fifth.

speaker: TICKET
text: Adrian stayed back, patient after discovering twice that my existence complicated his wagers. At the halfway point, the duke struck my rear quarter. Lightly. Deliberately. The Lamborghini moved toward the edge. I caught it. Nigga, I said, you want to make this personal in public? He hit me again.

speaker: TICKET
text: This time I let the car move farther, gave him the space he expected to take and watched him overcommit into it. His front wheels crossed the seam at the wrong angle. The black car bounced, lost its clean line and fell half a length behind. I took the center. The crowd on the fort's quay began screaming.

speaker: TICKET
text: We hit the final ramp together, blue and black climbing out of the sea. I landed first on the stone road, turned beneath the fort wall and headed back toward the second crossing. The duke followed. Close. He was furious now, but still good. That mattered. A bad driver could have excused himself. Aurelio knew exactly how well I was beating him.

speaker: TICKET
text: On the return crossing, a platform ahead of us shifted sharply. One of its holding boats had moved away. The floating road opened into a narrow gap. Not huge. Huge would have made the trap obvious enough for everybody to stop.

speaker: TICKET
text: This was the kind of gap meant to catch one car wrong and turn the rest of the race into a tragic discussion about conditions. I saw the duke look toward it. Then toward me. Nigga, there it was. I didn't call the thunder. I called his bluff. I stayed beside him. Closer.

speaker: TICKET
text: So close he could not change his line without hitting me hard enough for every camera to see the choice. The gap came toward us. His hands tightened on the wheel. He braked. I didn't. The Lamborghini left the edge, cleared the broken space and landed on the next platform with a crack that went through my teeth. The car stayed straight.

speaker: TICKET
text: Behind me, Aurelio's black machine hit the gap slower, nose dipping, rear wheels lifting before the front caught the far side. It landed badly. Its front bumper tore away. I kept going. The other drivers slowed and took the gap under the marshals' direction. The race wasn't over. The trap hadn't swallowed anybody.

speaker: TICKET
text: The duke had simply damaged his own car trying to arrange the shape of my fear. Nigga, expensive lesson. We came off the floating road onto the island circuit. The coast flashed past my windows. Villages, gardens, the opera house, the bakery where Julian's mother stood waving a blue cloth as I passed. Inez caught the duke before the palace hill. Cassius caught him after.

speaker: TICKET
text: Aurelio tried to hold them off. Couldn't. The black car's damaged front scraped at every dip, throwing sparks beneath the gold paint. He had enough speed to remain dangerous and not enough control to look graceful doing it. I crossed the finish first. Inez second. Cassius third. The duke came fourth, his car smoking, his face so still it looked painted.

speaker: TICKET
text: Sabine climbed out behind him and walked straight to me. I can confirm it, she said. What? You're impossible. Nigga, peer review. She laughed and shook my hand with both of hers. The sixth key was brought forward by Lord Orlan, who now looked like he had begun rehearsing a life in which he worked for somebody else.

speaker: TICKET
text: He held the cushion out at arm's length. I took the key. Behind him, the duke stepped out of his ruined car. The crowd booed. Not everybody. Enough. He looked up at the palace, then back at me. You haven't won the island. One more race. One more road. Nigga, I like roads. He came closer.

speaker: TICKET
text: For the first time there were no cameras between us, only at our sides. His voice dropped. I can make the island empty before you claim it. My smile went away. He saw it and thought he had found something useful. I can burn every car, sink every ship, silence every stage. You can arrive first to ashes.

speaker: TICKET
text: I looked at him for a long moment. Then I took the key off its ribbon and held it between two fingers. Nigga, you keep mistaking your last chance to walk away for suspense. His eyes hardened. I didn't raise my voice. You touch my people, your last race happens on foot. He stepped back. His guards closed around him.

speaker: TICKET
text: The crowd parted as he walked toward the palace gates. At the top of the steps stood the stranger in the dark uniform. This time the stranger smiled at me openly. Like he had enjoyed every second. Shawna came beside me. What'd he say? I told her. All of it.

speaker: TICKET
text: She looked toward the palace, then down at the six keys in the case Porsche held open beside us. Then we don't leave everybody here alone tonight. No. Nigga, good. We took over the opera house before sunset. Not by force.

speaker: TICKET
text: Valentina opened the doors and told us which rooms had beds, which corridors reached the street and which windows stuck when the sea wind turned. The company stayed. Workers brought food. Rocco sent supplies. Celadon kept the Sovereign Sun ready in the harbor, its lights bright, its crew finally working for a captain they trusted.

speaker: TICKET
text: Tank and Bruno stood at the main doors while people came and went. Mercedes and Porsche organized rooms with the efficiency of women who had spent their adult lives judging whether a strange building wanted anything good for them. Nero and Esteban sat with the old island mechanics, drawing the final race course from memory. No secret instructions.

speaker: TICKET
text: Just the shape of roads they loved and the places the duke had changed. Shawna rehearsed with Rosa and the full company. I stood in the back of the hall listening. Outside, the island waited for the night. Inside, my wife filled the room with a voice the duke had promised to silence. Nigga, he was going to have to come through me first.
